text: The CAS module has detected an internal fault in its own electronics.
hint: Often logged together with terminal 15 output faults (A0BE/A0BF/A0C0) and no-start or no-ignition symptoms; common cause is a failing CAS unit, but check battery voltage and CAS power/ground first.
notes: Sources describe BMW/MINI CAS (CAS3 is used in E9x) rather than a specific E90 thread. Not tied to a single component.

text: CAS internal register-monitoring fault; if it keeps recurring the CAS can block engine start and the steering lock.
hint: An E90 forum post links it to low voltage during cranking. Clear it, start with a charger/14 V supply connected and see if it returns; then check battery and main cables. Shops reset it with a CAS/ELV reset function.
notes: One E90 tool readout labels it simply as a CAS control-unit fault. OBDII365 and YouTube sources were attributed via titles.

text: CAS sees an implausible gear-selector position (Park/Neutral) input.
hint: Often stored without symptoms. If the car won't crank in P/N, check the selector/gearbox P-N signal and wiring to the CAS.
notes: Seen on an E90 335i and an E87 120d (same CAS family); e90-forum.de shows it as the P/N input fault in CAS.PRG.

text: CAS reports a problem with its own supply voltage (terminal 30 feed).
hint: Check battery condition, CAS fuses and the main positive cable connections before suspecting the CAS.
notes: Dekra report is from an E87 120d (shared CAS3 family); JustAnswer title attributes A0B2 to CAS supply on an E90 320d.

text: CAS sees a missing or faulty starter (terminal 50) signal.
hint: Check the starter solenoid wire, starter and battery cables; low battery voltage while cranking can also set it.
notes: Source 1 and the e90-forum thread 69649 are the same owner's readout; Dekra report is from an E87 120d.

text: CAS is not getting a valid road-speed signal.
hint: The speed comes over the CAN bus from the DSC; look for DSC or CAN faults stored at the same time.

text: CAS finds the road-speed signal implausible (its different inputs disagree).
hint: Usually a side effect of DSC/CAN or low-voltage problems; check for speed-related faults in other modules.

text: CAS reports a fault in the engine start (starter control) function.
notes: Both sources are general BMW/MINI CAS repair articles, not an E90 readout; wording is vague so kept at medium.

text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 1).
hint: Common pattern with A0A9 on a failing CAS, often when warm; check fuses and loads on the terminal 15 circuits first.
notes: Generic BMW/MINI CAS sources.

text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 2).
notes: Generic BMW/MINI CAS sources.

text: CAS reports a fault on one of its terminal 15 (ignition) outputs (output 3).
notes: Generic BMW/MINI CAS sources.

text: CAS reports a problem with the power supply to the electric steering lock.
hint: Check the steering lock fuse/feed and connector; a weak battery can also trigger steering lock faults.
notes: From an Autel scan report of a real E90 320i. This may overlap with the previously listed A111; I could not find any source confirming A111 as the steering-lock supply, so check that entry.

text: CAS reports a wiring/line fault to the electric steering lock.
notes: Seen on an E87 120d report (same CAS/ELV family). A114 is also named in a German E91 steering-lock no-start thread, without text.

text: CAS reports its K-CAN bus controller went bus-off.
hint: Usually one of many bus-off codes after a K-CAN wiring short or a failing module; check for the same code in other modules.
notes: Carly report, E93.

text: CAS reports a K-CAN low-wire physical bus fault.
notes: Carly report, E93.

text: The cluster got a faulty terminal-status (ignition state) message from the CAS on the CAN bus.
hint: Usually a side effect of low battery voltage, a CAS problem or a bus fault; check battery and main power connections and look for CAS faults.
notes: CAN message 0x130, sender CAS.

text: The cluster got a faulty or missing stability-control (DSC) status message on the CAN bus.
hint: Look at the DSC fault memory and its supply/CAN wiring; often appears with other DSC message faults.
notes: mini2.info gives message 0x19E from DSC; bmw-syndikat E90 thread (generic tool wording) says ABS/ESP message missing. One other E90 readout showed only generic text.

text: The cluster got a faulty door-status message from the CAS.
The cluster got a faulty engine-speed (RPM) message from the engine computer.
notes: CAN message 0x0AA, sender DME/DDE.

text: The cluster got a faulty engine-data message from the engine computer.
notes: CAN message 0x1D0, sender DME/DDE.

text: The cluster got a faulty speed set-point (cruise control) message from the engine side.
notes: CAN message 0x200. The e90-forum 69649 thread is the same owner's list.

text: The cluster got a faulty or missing distance-travelled message from the DSC.
The cluster got a faulty or missing vehicle-speed message from the DSC.
The cluster got a faulty message from the junction box (JBE).
notes: CAN message 0x0C0.

text: The cluster got a faulty message from the trailer module.
The cluster got a faulty or missing gear-shift indicator message from the engine computer.
The cluster got a faulty electric power steering message.
The cluster got a faulty auto start-stop (MSA) status message from the engine computer.
The cluster got a faulty lighting-status message from the footwell module (FRM).
hint: Commonly appears with A3C1 when the FRM has failed or lost its coding/data (lights, indicators and windows dead).

text: The cluster is not receiving a valid message from the footwell module (FRM).
hint: Check FRM fuses and power; a failed or corrupted FRM is a common cause.

text: The instrument cluster logged that its power supply was switched off or interrupted.
hint: Check battery voltage and the cluster supply; often logged after battery disconnects or low voltage.

text: The instrument cluster saw supply voltage that was too high or too low.
hint: Common cause: weak battery or charging problem.

text: The cluster reports a fault with the outside temperature sensor.
The cluster reports a fault with the left fuel level sender.
The cluster reports a fault with the right fuel level sender.
The cluster reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.
hint: Usually logged by many modules at once; look for a K-CAN short or a faulty module dragging the bus down.

text: The cluster's CAN controller went bus-off.
Footwell module reports the left front fog light circuit faulty (left daytime running light on M3).
hint: Check the bulb and connector first.

text: Footwell module reports the right front fog light circuit faulty (right daytime running light on M3).
hint: Check the bulb and connector first.

text: Footwell module reports the left daytime running light faulty.
hint: On cars with angel-eye DRLs check the ring bulb/LED and its connector.
notes: A8C5 also listed (no text) in an E90 readout on e90-forum.de.

text: Footwell module reports the right daytime running light faulty.
Footwell module reports the front left side-marker/parking light faulty (open circuit).
notes: One source calls it side marker, the other front left parking light.

text: Footwell module reports the right brake light faulty.
Footwell module reports the left brake light faulty.
Footwell module reports the left rear turn signal faulty.
Footwell module reports the third brake light / left adaptive brake light faulty.
Footwell module reports the third brake light / right adaptive brake light faulty.
Footwell module found an open circuit in a headlight height (vertical aim) adjuster motor.
hint: Check the headlight leveling motor and its connector.

text: Footwell module logged a flat/exhausted battery condition.
hint: Charge or test the battery; usually set after the car sat or was jump-started.

text: Footwell module switched off the parking/side lights to protect a discharging battery.
Footwell module reports a fault on light switch position 1.
Footwell module reports a fault on light switch position 2.
Footwell module lost communication with a LIN-bus control unit (such as the light switch).
Footwell module reports the terminal 15 (ignition on) signal is missing.
Footwell module lost communication with the driver-side mirror.
Footwell module lost communication with the passenger-side mirror.
Footwell module reports the driver-side mirror heater faulty.
Footwell module reports the driver-side mirror adjustment motor faulty.
Footwell module reports the passenger-side mirror adjustment motor faulty.
Footwell module reports the steering column left turn-signal switch input faulty.
notes: Same number as a KOMBI code with a different meaning; module matters.

text: Footwell module reports the steering column right turn-signal switch input faulty.
Footwell module reports the steering column high-beam/flasher switch input faulty.
Footwell module is not receiving the steering-angle message.
Footwell module is not receiving messages from the DSC.
Footwell module is not receiving the road-speed message from the DSC.
Footwell module reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.
Junction box reports a problem with the terminal 30g_f supply circuit.
hint: Terminal 30g_f feeds modules like the head unit; check the relay/fuses and battery state.
notes: Both sources attributed via thread titles.

text: Junction box reports that its power supply was interrupted.
notes: Seen on E87 120d report (same JBE family).

text: Junction box is not receiving the terminal-status message from the CAS.
Junction box reports a PT-CAN communication fault.
Junction box reports its K-CAN controller went bus-off.
Junction box reports PT-CAN bus-off / K-CAN running on a single wire.
Junction box reports a fault in the A/C compressor control valve circuit.
notes: Owner listed it under central body (JBE); the e90-forum 69649 thread is the same owner's list.

text: Roof function centre reports a fault with the windscreen condensation (fogging) sensor.
hint: Often the sensor behind the mirror has come loose or its connector is bad; replacing the FZD or rain sensor alone may not fix it.

text: Roof function centre reports a fault in the front interior light circuit.
hint: Check the front interior/reading lamps and their wiring in the roof console.
notes: Only source is an Autel scan report of an E87 120d (same FZD family as E9x); no E90-specific confirmation found.

text: Roof function centre reports a sunroof mechanism fault.
notes: E87 120d report, shared FZD.

text: Roof function centre reports a fault with the sunroof switch.
notes: E87 120d report, shared FZD.

text: Sunroof needs or failed its normalization (initialization).
hint: Common after battery disconnects; re-initialize the sunroof by holding the switch.

text: Climate control reports a fault on the 12 V supply to the centre console switch centre.
Climate control got a faulty or missing terminal-status message from the CAS.
Climate control reports a K-CAN wiring fault.
Climate control's CAN controller went bus-off.
Park distance control reports a K-CAN low-wire or interruption fault.
Park distance control reports its CAN controller went bus-off.
Head unit's stored list of fitted modules doesn't match the car's target configuration.
hint: Often appears after retrofits or coding; usually harmless if nothing is missing.
notes: Seen on CCC-equipped cars.

text: Head unit failed to wake the bus/network after three attempts.
notes: CCC, E93.

text: Head unit reports a K-CAN bus-off/communication fault.
notes: CCC, E93.

text: Head unit reports a K-CAN low-wire fault.
notes: CCC, E93.

text: Airbag module is not receiving the vehicle-speed message from the DSC.
Rain/light sensor saw supply voltage that was too high or too low.
notes: Logged as a separate RLS entry on an E90 335i report; address not known.

text: Engine computer's power management logged a battery problem.
hint: Test the battery and make sure a replacement was registered with the right type/capacity.

text: Engine computer lost communication with the intelligent battery sensor (IBS).
hint: Check the IBS on the battery negative terminal and its wire.

text: Engine computer reports a communication problem with the alternator.
Power management detected too much current draw while the car was asleep (parasitic drain).
hint: Look for a module keeping the car awake; in that thread the tailgate wiring harness was damaged.
